3.2 — Projectiles: Instantiate, Fire, Destroy

Your turret knows when you are near; now it needs teeth. Spawning and firing a projectile looks complex, but it breaks down into four smaller sub-problems: spawn a prefab → point it at the player → move it through space → destroy it when done. Today, you read Unity's projectile functions and build Projectile.cs from scratch.

Read the Docs ~15 min

Firing a projectile requires coordinating several distinct Unity functions. Read how the engine handles each step:

Sub-ProblemUnity FunctionDocumentation & Purpose
1. Spawning Instantiate(prefab, pos, rot) Creates a brand-new clone of a prefab at runtime and places it into the scene hierarchy.
2. Aiming (target - origin).normalized Vector subtraction produces a vector pointing toward the target. .normalized reduces its length to 1.
3. Moving transform.Translate or Rigidbody2D Moves the bullet every frame along its forward direction.
4. Cleanup Destroy(gameObject, delay) Destroys the projectile after a time delay (seconds) to prevent off-screen bullets from clogging memory.

Socratic: Evaluating Multiple Ways to Move Projectiles

Compare these two ways to move a projectile across the screen:

  • Method 1 (Translate): transform.Translate(Vector3.right * speed * Time.deltaTime);
  • Method 2 (Physics Velocity): GetComponent<Rigidbody2D>().linearVelocity = direction * speed;
  1. If you want bullets that bounce off stone walls like in a pinball or billiards game, which method (Method 1 or Method 2) is significantly easier, and why?
  2. If your projectiles are laser beams, energy arrows, or magic missiles that fly straight through obstacles, why is Method 1 clean and lightweight?
  3. Why is Destroy(gameObject, 5f) called an essential garbage collection pattern? What would happen to your game's framerate if a player dodged 1,000 bullets and they all kept flying into deep space forever?
Read Function-Level Examples ~15 min

Notice how each mathematical, rotational, and spawning function works in isolation across completely different game systems:

Example 1 — Computing Direction and Unit Length on an Airplane Navigation System:

// Vector subtraction (destination - current) gives direction; .normalized scales length to 1.0
Vector3 headingDirection = (waypointPosition - transform.position).normalized;

Example 2 — Converting 2D Direction to Angle on a Weather Vane:

// Atan2 calculates the angle in radians from X/Y coordinates; Rad2Deg converts to 0-360 degrees
float windAngle = Mathf.Atan2(windVector.y, windVector.x) * Mathf.Rad2Deg;

Example 3 — Applying 2D Rotation with Quaternion.AngleAxis:

// In 2D games, rotation occurs around the Z axis (Vector3.forward, pointing out of the screen)
transform.rotation = Quaternion.AngleAxis(windAngle, Vector3.forward);

Example 4 — Spawning and Initializing on a Magic Fountain:

// 1. Stamp clone into world
GameObject orb = Instantiate(orbPrefab, fountainNozzle.position, Quaternion.identity);

// 2. Access component on the fresh clone and pass setup data
orb.GetComponent<MagicOrb>().InitializeOrb(targetCoords);

Example 5 — Timed Cleanup with Destroy on a Floating Soap Bubble:

// Schedules this GameObject to be automatically destroyed 4 seconds after appearing
Destroy(gameObject, 4.0f);

Predict Before Building

  1. In Example 1, what happens if you forget .normalized? If the target is 20 units away, how does that affect any math multiplied by that direction?
  2. In Example 3, why is Vector3.forward (0, 0, 1) used as the axis of rotation for a 2D sprite?
  3. In Example 5, why is scheduling destruction with a timer better than never destroying dodged projectiles?
Build Lab: Your Turn ~25 min
Architectural Specification for Projectile.cs:

Variables & Tuning Knobs:

  • Where in Assets/Scripts/ should you create this script, and what must the class name match?
  • What serialized float knobs should designers be able to adjust in the Inspector for bullet speed and maximum time-to-live? What defaults make sense?

Aiming & Initialization:

  • When a projectile is spawned, it needs to know where the target was standing. What public method signature can receive that target coordinate?
  • How do you calculate a direction vector from where the bullet spawned to where the target is? Why must this vector be normalized?
  • What trigonometric function calculates the angle in radians from X and Y components? How do you convert radians into degrees?
  • Which 3D axis represents the pivot axis for 2D rotation? What Quaternion method builds a rotation from an angle and an axis?
  • How do you tell Unity to automatically clean up this bullet after its lifetime expires, even if it never hits a target?

Per-Frame Flight in Update:

  • Since the projectile was rotated to face the target upon spawn, which local direction represents "forward" in Unity 2D sprite geometry?
  • What function moves the transform each frame? How do you ensure flight speed is frame-rate independent?
  • Which prefab in Assets/Prefabs/ needs this script attached?
Architectural Specification for TurretController.cs:

Inspector Slots:

  • What serialized fields are needed so designers can drag in the projectile prefab and assign the physical spawn nozzle?

Attack Method:

  • In your firing function, what guard check ensures the prefab and spawn point slots are not left unassigned?
  • What method stamps a new clone of the projectile prefab into the scene? Where should it be placed, and what rotation should it start with?
  • How do you grab the Projectile script on that newly created clone? What method do you call on it to aim it at the player's position?

Triggering the Attack:

  • Inside your range check in Update(), where should this attack method be invoked?
  • What slots need to be connected in the Turret's Inspector before testing in Play mode?

Save and press Play. Walk near the turret. A projectile spawns from the muzzle, aims at your position, and shoots across the screen! (Notice that it fires 60 bullets every second — in lesson 3.3 we fix the cooldown!)

Bug Hunt: Projectile Errors

  1. What happens if you leave the Projectile Prefab slot unassigned in the Inspector? What error does Unity throw when you step in range?
  2. In Projectile.cs, what happens if you change Vector3.right to Vector3.up in Update()? Which direction do bullets fly relative to their aim?
  3. In Projectile.cs, comment out the Destroy(gameObject, lifetime) line. Fire several bullets and watch the Hierarchy in play mode. Do the spawned instances ever leave the scene?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Bullet Tuning

  1. In the Turret_Projectile prefab, tune speed between 3 (slow dodgeable dodgeball) and 15 (bullet-hell sniper). How does projectile speed alter the player's emotional reaction to the turret?
  2. Why does Initialize calculate the direction once, instead of continuously updating direction in Update()? What kind of weapon would you get if direction re-aimed toward the player every frame?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Break down projectile firing into instantiation, aiming, translation, and destruction
  • Explain the role of Instantiate() in stamping runtime prefab clones
  • Explain why vectors are normalized before calculating angle and movement
  • Create Projectile.cs and wire the turret's projectile spawn slots
  • Commit your projectile system to GitHub
